title: Every FPV pack tool keeps a path through FPVBuddy's MCP server
goal: No FPV function is lost: each NERV FPV tool calls FPVBuddy over MCP or stays in NERV for a stated reason
acceptance: batteries.list, batteries.chat, batteries.due, batteries.resistance and fleet.chat call FPVBuddy's MCP tools; writes (charge state, resistance, crashes) go through FPVBuddy write tools gated as actions needing approval
fleet.print stays in NERV (printing, F-121) and reads the fleet over MCP; printed-part and print-job data stay with F-121 keyed by FPVBuddy drone IDs

fpv.blackbox_report moves to FPVBuddy as a stateless analyzer tool; fpv.import_build, fpv.add_doc and fpv.wiring_answer move to FPVBuddy with the builds and manufacturer docs (src/blackbox.ts, src/fpv-builds.ts, src/diyfpv-build.ts); FPVBuddy's backlog owns those tools, and this step starts only when they exist

Unreachable FPVBuddy: NERV says so clearly in chat and Telegram (which tool, that the data is in FPVBuddy, retry later), never a silent failure or an empty list; a test covers it with a stopped fake server
A join test runs a chat phrase per tool through a fake FPVBuddy MCP server and back
privacy: Owner fleet data stays local-only and never enters Git; tests use invented batteries, drones, crashes and photos.
escalation: A material scope or effort increase goes to the owner
A new MCP write permission goes to the owner before it is enabled

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-26 after the owner decision (reroute ten tools to MCP calls, the unreachable message and per-tool join tests). Not a measurement.
